title: The Weekend Weather

lines.text: Good morning, it's eight o'clock on Radio Sunshine. Now let's see what the weather is going to do this weekend. Tom, what's the forecast?
Morning, Emma. Well, look at those dark clouds in the west. It's going to rain this afternoon, so take an umbrella if you're going out.
Oh no. And tonight?
Tonight the rain will stop around midnight, and I think it'll be quite cold. Temperatures will drop to about five degrees.
What about Saturday? I'm going to have a barbecue with my family.
Good news for you. Saturday will be dry and sunny in most places. It'll probably be the best day of the weekend, with temperatures of around twenty-two degrees.
Perfect! I'll buy the sausages today, then.
But on Saturday evening the wind is going to get stronger, so don't leave anything light in the garden.
Thanks for the warning. And Sunday?
Sunday won't be so nice, I'm afraid. There's a big storm over the sea right now, and it's moving towards us. It's going to arrive on Sunday morning.
So, no picnic on Sunday?
No, I don't think it'll be a good day for a picnic. Maybe a good day for a film at home.
Great advice. I'll talk to you again at nine. Thanks, Tom.

title: Before the Final

lines.text: Laura, are you coming to watch the final on Sunday?
I don't know. If I finish my project on Saturday, I'll come. Where are you going to watch it?
At my brother's house. He has a huge TV. If you come, I'll make my famous chicken wings.
Then I'll definitely finish my project! So, do you think Deportivo Andino will win?
I hope so. If Ramírez plays, we'll win easily. He's our best player.
But he hurt his knee last week. What'll happen if he doesn't play?
If he doesn't play, it'll be very difficult. Real Caribe has a really strong defense.
And what will you do if Andino wins?
If we win, I'll paint my face green and white and go to the city center with everybody.
Ha! And if they lose?
If they lose, I won't talk to anybody for a week.
That's a bit dramatic, Diego! Okay, what time does it start?
At four. If you get there early, you'll get the best seat on the sofa.
Deal. If it rains, I'll take a taxi. See you on Sunday!

title: First Salsa Class
focus: Gerunds after like / love / hate / enjoy

lines.text: Welcome to Salsa Viva! I'm Marta. Is this your first class?
Yes, it is. I'm Kevin, from Melbourne. I'm on holiday in Cali for a month.
Great. So, do you like dancing?
I love listening to salsa music, but I'm not very good at dancing. I hate looking silly in front of people.
Don't worry. Nobody looks silly here. What do you enjoy doing in your free time?
I enjoy running and swimming. I really like doing sport, so I'm quite fit.
That helps a lot. Salsa is good exercise. Do you mind dancing with different partners?
No, I don't mind. Actually, I like meeting new people.
Perfect. In this class, we change partners every ten minutes. Many of our students love practising with someone new.
And what about the steps? I'm terrible at remembering things.
We start slowly. First, you learn the basic step. Most beginners enjoy learning it because it's easy.
Sounds good. Do I need special shoes?
No, just comfortable ones. But don't wear trainers, because they stick to the floor. Most people hate dancing in trainers.
Okay. I can't wait to start!

title: Our New Recycling System
focus: Sequence adverbs (first, then, after that, finally)

lines.text: Hello, everyone. This is Martin, the building manager. I'm going to explain how our new recycling system works.
From next Monday, there are three new bins in the car park: a green one, a blue one and a black one.
First, wash your bottles and tins with a little water. They must be clean, or the recycling company won't take them.
Then, put all plastic bottles, tins and cartons in the blue bin.
After that, take your paper and cardboard and put it in the green bin. Please fold the big boxes first.
Next, put food waste, like fruit and vegetables, in the small brown box in your kitchen. You'll find one outside your door this weekend.
When the brown box is full, empty it into the black bin downstairs.
Finally, put everything else, like old clothes or broken toys, in the normal rubbish room, not in the new bins.
Glass is different. Please take glass bottles to the big container on the corner of the street.
The recycling lorry comes on Tuesdays and Fridays, early in the morning.
If you have any questions, you can find me in the office on the ground floor, from nine to five.
Thank you for helping. Together, we can make our building greener.

title: What Did You See?

lines.text: Good afternoon. I'm Officer Wilson. You saw the accident this morning, is that right?
Yes, I did. I was waiting for the bus outside the bakery.
What time was it?
About half past eight. It was raining a little, and a lot of people were walking to work.
Okay. Can you tell me what happened?
Well, a young man was riding his bike along the street. He was wearing headphones, I think.
And the car?
A white car was coming out of the supermarket car park. The driver was looking at her phone, so she didn't see the bike.
Did the car hit the bike?
Yes, but not very hard. The cyclist fell off and dropped his bag. Some people ran to help him.
Was he hurt?
He hurt his arm, but he stood up quickly. While the driver was calling an ambulance, a shop assistant brought him a chair and some water.
Thank you. Was anyone else in the car?
Yes, a little dog was sitting in the back seat. It was barking the whole time!
Thanks very much. That's really helpful.

title: Life Before Mobile Phones

lines.text: Welcome back to Family Stories. Today my guest is my grandfather, Luis. Grandpa, what was life like before cell phones?
Very different, Ana! When I was young, we didn't use to have a phone at home. Only one family on our street had one.
So how did you use to call people?
We used to go to the store on the corner. There was a public phone there, and you used to pay with coins.
And how did you meet your friends?
We used to make plans at school. If you said four o'clock in the park, you had to be there at four. Nobody could send a message to say they were late.
That sounds stressful!
Not really. I think people used to arrive on time more often.
Did you use to write letters?
Oh yes. I used to write to your grandmother every week when she studied in Bogotá. Her letters used to take five days to arrive.
Five days! What about photos?
We used to take photos with a camera and wait a week for the store to print them. Sometimes half of them were bad.
Do you miss those days?
Sometimes. But now I can see your face on a video call every Sunday, and I love that.

title: Swimming Pool Rules
focus: Modals of obligation (have to, must, don't have to)

lines.text: Good morning and welcome to the Riverside Sports Center swimming pool. Please listen to some important information.
All swimmers must take a shower before they get into the pool.
You have to wear a swimming cap in the water. If you don't have one, you can buy one at reception for three dollars.
You don't have to bring a towel. Free towels are available next to the changing rooms.
Children under eight must be with an adult at all times.
You mustn't run near the pool, because the floor is very wet.
Food and drinks are not allowed in the pool area. You have to eat in the café on the first floor.
From Monday to Friday, lanes one and two are for fast swimmers only. You don't have to swim fast in the other lanes.
If you want to use the diving board, you have to ask a lifeguard first.
Today, the small pool is closed for cleaning, so families have to use the main pool until four o'clock.
You don't have to book for the evening classes this week. Just come along at seven.
Have a great swim, and remember: if you need help, please talk to one of our lifeguards in red T-shirts.
